public_rationale: JLL places a typical 50 MW build at 18 months, consistent with part of the claim. SynMax finds that larger projects can complete as quickly as smaller ones. Neither source measures whether larger projects miss their original schedules more often. The combined claim therefore remains unsettled.
limitations: A duration estimate for one facility size cannot establish the range across all types.
Construction duration and schedule reliability cannot be substituted for one another.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Across the board, the message seems to be that it takes about 18 to 24 months to build any kind of data center, and that the bigger they are, the less likely they are to be completed on schedule.

statement.excerpt: Across the board, the message seems to be fairly simple: it takes about 18 to 24 months to build any kind of data center, and the bigger they are, the less likely they are to get completed on schedule.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: the bigger they are, the less likely they are to get completed on schedule
our_interpretation: Read as a general description of typical construction times, rather than an exceptionless minimum.
Measure construction from groundbreaking to operational readiness. Distinguish an operational phase from completion of an entire campus.
The contextual construction cycle runs from October 2023 through publication on May 12, 2026.
The size claim concerns missing originally announced completion dates. Longer construction times alone do not establish more schedule failures.
criteria.support_condition: Representative project records show typical construction lasting approximately 18–24 months across facility types, and lower on-time completion rates for larger projects.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative comparable records show typical durations materially outside that range, or show that larger projects do not have lower on-time completion rates.

evidence.explanation: The review tracked 138 projects scheduled for 2025 and found that larger facilities could complete as quickly as smaller ones. This challenges the implied size disadvantage, but duration is not the same measure as adherence to an original deadline.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative project dataset linking size and facility type to groundbreaking, original deadlines, and actual operational completion, with phases identified separately.
